summary: This Dockerfile builds a minimal Python 3.14 image in two stages: first it installs the markitdown library with document parsing support into an isolated directory, then it creates a final lightweight image that copies only those dependencies and runs as an unprivileged user for security. The multi-stage approach keeps the final image small by discarding the build tools after installation.

explanations.1: This special comment tells Docker to use an experimental version of the Dockerfile syntax that includes advanced features like build caching.
explanations.3: The 'AS builder' creates a named intermediate stage that we'll reference later; we use it to install dependencies without bloating the final image.
explanations.6: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE prevents Python from creating .pyc cache files, which saves space in the image.
explanations.7: PYTHONUNBUFFERED makes Python send output directly rather than buffering it, which is important in containers where you want to see logs immediately.
explanations.8: PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK skips the automatic check for pip updates, making installations faster in a container.
explanations.13: This RUN command mounts a cache directory so pip can reuse downloaded packages across Docker builds, speeding up rebuilds.
explanations.14: The --prefix=/python flag installs the package and its dependencies into a specific folder rather than system-wide, making it easy to copy to the final stage.
explanations.16: This starts a fresh image without the build tools; we only copy the pre-installed Python packages from the builder stage.
explanations.22: PYTHONPATH tells Python where to find installed packages, pointing to the copied isolated directory from the builder stage.
explanations.23: PATH is updated to include the bin folder from our isolated Python install so we can run Python executables directly.
explanations.25: ARG defines build-time arguments with defaults; UID and GID are used when creating the user account.
explanations.29: groupadd creates a user group; the curly braces reference the GID argument passed at build time.
explanations.30: useradd creates an unprivileged user account with no login shell, which improves security by preventing direct shell access.
explanations.32: COPY --from=builder copies only the installed packages from the builder stage, leaving behind all the build tools and bloat.
explanations.36: USER switches to running as the unprivileged developer user instead of root, preventing containers from having full system access.
explanations.39: ENTRYPOINT sets the default command, so running the container automatically executes the markitdown CLI tool.
